title: Doping with donors and acceptors, carrier concentrations

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
Doping replaces a tiny fraction of silicon atoms with impurities. A **donor** (column V, e.g. phosphorus) has five valence electrons; four bond and the fifth is loosely held and is freed at room temperature, leaving a fixed positive ion. An **acceptor** (column III, e.g. boron) has only three, so it grabs an electron from a neighbouring bond, creating a mobile hole and a fixed negative ion.

Doping of even one part per million swamps \(n_i\), so the majority carrier concentration is set by the doping and the minority concentration follows from the mass-action law. When both types are present they **compensate**: only the net doping matters.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
Charge neutrality: \(p_0 - n_0 + N_D - N_A = 0\).
n-type (\(N_D \gg n_i\)):
\[ n_0 \approx N_D, \qquad p_0 = \frac{n_i^2}{N_D} \]
p-type (\(N_A \gg n_i\)):
\[ p_0 \approx N_A, \qquad n_0 = \frac{n_i^2}{N_A} \]
Compensated, \(N_D > N_A\): \(n_0 \approx N_D - N_A\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
A sample has \(N_D = 8\times10^{15}\) and \(N_A = 3\times10^{15}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}\).
Net doping is n-type: \(n_0 \approx 5\times10^{15}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}\).
\[ p_0 = \frac{10^{20}}{5\times10^{15}} = 2\times10^{4}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}} \]
The minority holes are outnumbered by about \(2.5\times10^{11}\) to one.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Adding \(N_D\) and \(N_A\) instead of subtracting them.
- Thinking a doped sample is electrically charged. The ions are balanced by the carriers.
- Using \(n_0 \approx N_D\) when the doping is comparable to \(n_i\) (then solve the quadratic).
- Swapping which impurity column gives donors versus acceptors.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Majority and minority concentrations set conductivity, junction potentials and diode currents. Every PN junction and MOS problem starts by writing down \(n_0\) and \(p_0\) on each side, exactly as above.
